I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way for me to use my irrigated land and protect total grain output. I have farmed for many years, so I do not want to spread myself too thin with too much cotton, especially since some people in my household work off-farm and labor has to be used carefully. I will still keep a smaller cotton area, because it helps me diversify income and I already know how to manage it, but I will not let it take over the farm. On the wheat-maize land, I will use better seed and fairly solid fertilizer rates because I have well irrigation and I want stable yields rather than gambling on low input. For maize, I will mostly follow wheat with a no-tillage or light direct-seeding approach to save time in the busy season. For cotton, I will give more attention to water, potash, and pest control, because that crop is more management-heavy and I only want as much as I can handle well.
